stories.headline: Iran launches sustained drone and missile campaign against UAE; air defenses intercept hundreds of projectiles
stories.summary: Since late April/early May 2026, Iran has conducted repeated missile and drone strikes on the UAE, with Emirati air defenses reportedly intercepting 551 ballistic missiles, 29 cruise missiles, and 2,265 drones as of May 10. The UAE has reported 13 deaths and 230 wounded since attacks began, blamed Iran for the strikes, reserved its right to respond, and continued to engage projectiles on May 10 including two UAVs shot down on the analysis date.

stories.headline: Iran drones strike ADNOC oil tanker Barakah in Strait of Hormuz on May 4
stories.summary: On May 4, Iran struck an empty ADNOC crude oil tanker (M.V. Barakah) with two drones while it transited the Strait of Hormuz, with no injuries reported. The UAE described the attack as terrorism and a violation of UN Resolution 2817, reserving the right to respond.

stories.headline: UAE exits OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1, triggering geopolitical realignment debate
stories.summary: The UAE formally withdrew from OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1, 2026, with ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber framing the move as serving the UAE's long-term strategic and economic interests. The exit prompted widespread analysis of a deepening Saudi-UAE rift, potential further withdrawals from the Arab League and GCC, and Abu Dhabi's emerging independent foreign policy trajectory aligned with Israel and the US.

stories.headline: ADNOC uses 'dark shipping' tactics to push LNG and crude through blocked Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: ADNOC has been disabling AIS transponders on tankers and using ship-to-ship transfers and multiple routing workarounds to move oil and LNG through the Strait of Hormuz since Iran effectively closed the waterway. At least two LNG tankers (Mubaraz, Mraweh) successfully crossed the strait, and ADNOC exported roughly 6 million barrels of crude in April using these methods, though total flows remain far below pre-war levels.

stories.headline: G42-Microsoft $1 billion Kenya data center stalls over power constraints and payment disputes
stories.summary: A flagship $1 billion data center project near Olkaria, Kenya, announced by Microsoft and UAE-based G42 in 2024, has effectively stalled after President Ruto acknowledged the national grid cannot support the facility's power demands and negotiations broke down over the government's refusal to provide guaranteed annual capacity payments. Kenya's government subsequently disputed reports of a full suspension, saying the project remains on track.

stories.headline: ADNOC announces $55 billion project pipeline and unconventional oil/gas expansion post-OPEC exit
stories.summary: Following the UAE's OPEC exit, ADNOC announced AED 200 billion ($55 billion) in project awards planned for 2026–2028, spanning upstream and downstream operations, while its upstream CEO confirmed the company will make a final investment decision this year on an unconventional gas project with TotalEnergies.
